Name: DualSub Two Subtitle Languages for Language Learning
Author: feelSmooth
Description:
================================================================
STARDEW VALLEY - DualSub
Read the whole game in two languages at once, sentence by
sentence, for people learning a language while they play
================================================================

Every line a villager speaks, every cutscene, every letter in your
mailbox gets a second language with it.

It works SENTENCE BY SENTENCE. Each sentence in the language you know
is followed straight away by the same sentence in the language you are
learning, and in conversation each pair gets its own box:

    Hello!  »  Merhaba!
    You must be @.  »  Sen @ olmalısın.

so you never have to hold a paragraph in your head to find out what a
line meant, and no box is ever too full to read.

You choose BOTH languages, and any of the 12 can be either one - 120
combinations, all of them complete.

You also choose HOW MUCH gets doubled, from just the villagers'
dialogue up to every menu and item name in the game. The installer
remembers your answer, so the next time you only have to press Enter.

This mod contains no game text of its own. Stardew Valley installs all
twelve languages for everyone, so the installer reads your own copy of
the game and builds the two-language text on your PC. That is why the
download is a few tens of KB instead of hundreds of megabytes, why
every combination is available, and why it still works after a game
update.


---------------- BEFORE YOU START ------------------------------

You need Python. It is free, safe, made by python.org, and you install
it once:

  WINDOWS  https://www.python.org/downloads/  -> the big yellow
            "Download Python" button. In its installer, TICK THE BOX
            "Add python.exe to PATH" before clicking Install.

  LINUX    you almost certainly have it already. If not:
              Ubuntu / Debian / Mint  sudo apt install python3
              Fedora / Nobara          sudo dnf install python3
              Arch / CachyOS          sudo pacman -S python
            Steam Deck already has it - use Desktop Mode.

This mod is one Python file. It downloads nothing and installs nothing
on your PC. Everything it does is to the game's own files, and it can
put those back exactly as they were.

You do NOT need SMAPI, and this does not conflict with it.


---------------- INSTALL ---------------------------------------

  1. Close the game.

  2. Unzip this download somewhere you can find again - your Desktop
    or Downloads folder is fine.

  3. Open a command window IN that folder:

    WINDOWS  open the folder, click the white address bar at the top
              of the window, type  cmd  and press Enter.

    LINUX    right-click inside the folder and choose "Open Terminal
              Here" (most file managers have it).

  4. Type this and press Enter:

    WINDOWS      python dualsub_installer.py
    LINUX        python3 dualsub_installer.py

  5. The first time only, it asks where the game is. Paste the folder
    that holds the Content folder - or drag that folder from the file
    manager onto the window. It remembers the answer.

  6. Answer three questions: which language you play in, which one you
    want to learn, and which kinds of text to double.

  7. It works for a couple of seconds, says DONE, and tells you which
    language to pick in the game.

That is the whole installation. There is nothing to build, nothing to
copy by hand, no mod manager, and no files to replace.

IF WINDOWS SAYS IT CANNOT WRITE TO THE GAME FILES, the game is in
Program Files and needs administrator rights:

  * Click Start, type  cmd
  * Right-click "Command Prompt" and choose "Run as administrator"
  * Type  cd /d  then a space, then drag the unzipped folder onto the
    window, then press Enter
  * Then:  python dualsub_installer.py

Games installed on another drive (a Steam library on D:, say) usually
do not need this at all.


---------------- SET THE GAME'S LANGUAGE -----------------------

The last thing the installer prints is the language to choose. Start
the game, open Options, and pick it from the language list.

MOST OF THE TIME this is simply the language you play in. English
with Turkish means you pick English.

BUT IF THE LANGUAGE YOU ARE LEARNING is Japanese, Korean, Russian or
Chinese, you pick THAT one instead. Those four scripts can only be
drawn while their own font is loaded, and Stardew loads one font at a
time. The language you play in still comes first everywhere - only the
menu entry you click is different.

The installer prints the right answer either way, so you never have to
work this out yourself.


---------------- REMOVE ----------------------------------------

Run the installer again and press R.

It puts back every file it touched, byte for byte, from the copies it
made in the DualSub-Backup folder inside your game folder. Then it
deletes that folder and its own notes, and the game is exactly as it
was before.

You can also just verify the game files through Steam or GOG. That
replaces everything the mod changed and costs nothing.


---------------- WHICH COMBINATIONS WORK -----------------------

These eight share one alphabet and can be mixed freely, in either
direction, with nothing else changed:

    English      German      Spanish      French
    Hungarian    Italian      Portuguese  Turkish

These four each bring their own font:

    Japanese    Korean      Russian      Chinese

Each of the four pairs with any of the eight, in either direction -
you just pick the non-Latin one in the game's language menu.

TWO OF THE FOUR TOGETHER IS THE ONE THING THAT CANNOT WORK. Japanese
with Chinese, Russian with Korean, and so on: the game loads one font
at a time and no single font in it holds both scripts. The installer
lists those under "Not possible" rather than letting you pick one and
be disappointed.

That is 120 of the 132 possible orderings.

A FEW ACCENTS CHANGE SHAPE when a Latin language is paired with
Japanese or Korean, because those two fonts were built without them. German
umlauts are written out - Grüße becomes Gruesse - and other languages
lose the mark, so café reads as cafe. Nothing is ever dropped, and no
pair among the eight Latin languages is touched at all.


---------------- WHAT GETS DOUBLED -----------------------------

Step 3 is a list of switches. Type a number to turn one on or off,
press Enter when it looks right. Your answer is remembered, so next
time you can go straight through with Enter.

    Villager dialogue                            ON
      Everything the villagers say to you, indoors and out,
      plus phone calls and the Desert Festival.

    Cutscenes and festivals                      ON
      Story scenes, heart events, the festival days, the wedding
      and the letter Grandpa leaves you.

    Letters, notes and TV                        ON
      Mail, secret notes, and the television channels.

    Quests, bundles, awards                      ON
      Quest text, bundle names and achievement descriptions.

    Item and creature names                      ON
      Names and descriptions of items, crops, animals, monsters.

    Places and buildings                        ON
      Location names, map labels and building descriptions.

    Menus and system messages                    off
      Buttons, options, tooltips and what the game prints at you.

The last one is off because the interface is where doubling can do
harm. Turn it on if you want it; turn any of them off any time.

A LABEL IS NEVER DOUBLED, wherever it lives. "Name", "Skip Intro",
"Acc.", "Mon", "am", "spring" and the like sit in slots the game
measured for one language, and putting a second one there pushes them
over whatever is beside them. DualSub only doubles a value that is a
sentence, so the character screen, the clock and the calendar keep
their shape even with everything switched on. The words the game picks
at random to build sentences from are left alone for the same reason.

HOW A PAIR IS LAID OUT depends on what is drawing it. Conversation
boxes cannot hold a line break at all - the game reads that character
as something else entirely - so there the two sentences sit side by
side with a marker between them, one pair to a box. Letters, notes,
signs and the opening story can, so there the translation goes on the
line directly below, and a letter reads as alternating lines.


---------------- GOOD TO KNOW ----------------------------------

YOUR SAVES ARE NOT TOUCHED. This mod only ever writes inside the
game's Content folder, and it keeps a copy of everything it changes.

NOTHING IS EVER DOWNLOADED. The mod ships no text and no fonts. When a
pair needs a wider font, it copies one the game already has - Stardew's
own French/Hungarian/Turkish font file - and puts the original back on
removal.

A GAME UPDATE may replace some of the files DualSub wrote. If that
happens, removing the mod leaves those particular files as the update
left them and tells you so, rather than putting an out-of-date file
back on top of a new one.

MULTIPLAYER: the text is on your screen only. Other players see their
own game normally.

ABOUT 10,900 pieces of text get a second language with the switches as
they come, 11,400 with everything on, and 4,500 with dialogue alone.
Conversations gain roughly 4,200 extra boxes, which is the point: one
click per sentence pair instead of a wall of text.


---------------- IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG -----------------------

"python is not recognised"
    Python is not installed, or the PATH box was not ticked during its
    installation. Install it again from python.org and tick the box.

"That folder does not look like Stardew Valley"
    Point it at the folder that CONTAINS the Content folder, not at
    Content itself.

The game shows one language only
    You have not picked the right language in Options yet. Run the
    installer again - the top of its first screen prints the one to
    choose.

Boxes or blanks instead of letters
    Should not happen; the installer checks every character against
    the font before it writes anything. If you do see it, remove the
    mod and say which two languages you picked.

Anything else
    Run the installer and press R. That puts the game back. If it
    wrote dualsub-error.log next to the script, that file says what
    happened.

---------------- THE DUALSUB PROJECT & SUPPORT -----------------
The ultimate goal of DualSub is to break down language barriers in gaming by making dual-language subtitles a standard feature. Video games are one of the most engaging, effective ways to learn a new language, and this project exists to make that journey smooth, accessible, and fun for everyone.

Because every engine handles text differently, each game requires dedicated reverse-engineering. Creating a new parser means I need hands-on access to the game itself to test its file structures locally.

If you believe in this mission and want to help bring DualSub to more titles:
- Drop a request in the Posts tab so I know which games you're eager to learn with.
- Straight donations are warmly welcomed via the official Donation button above (PayPal).

Every single contribution goes directly toward acquiring new games and funding development tools. While support helps prioritize which titles get researched next, please keep in mind that future ports can never be guaranteed; they depend entirely on technical feasibility and available time. Rest assured, every DualSub mod will always remain 100% free for everyone.

Thank you so much to everyone downloading, sharing, and learning with this mod. Whether you're mastering a second language or polishing a third, your support and feedback make this whole project worth it!
